REFUTED by wire shape. The tally reads `final json = event.data['detail_json']; final map = json is Map ? json : const {};` (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/node_exposure_tally.dart:167-168). Production delivers a JSON *String*: native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/sequencer/event_translation.rs:174 `serde_json::to_string(detail)` -> bridge/src/event/sequencer.rs:128 `detail_json: String` -> event_mapping.dart:534 `'detail_json': sequencerEvent.detailJson`. Every other consumer decodes it first (event_operations.dart:316 `_decodeStructuredProgressJson` -> jsonDecode at :521). The shipped pin feeds a Map (exposure_card_wave_f_events_test.dart:66-68 `{'frame': frame, 'total': total}`), so it passes on a shape production never sends. Throwaway test (/tmp/.../scratchpad/refute_tally_test.dart, run in packages/skotiq_core): with detail_json = jsonEncode({'frame':N,'total':4}) the tally after four frames printed `WIRE-SHAPE tally after 4 frames: {}` (expected 4, got null); the same events with a Map printed `MAP-SHAPE tally: {node-one: NodeExposureTally(4/4)}`. At HEAD the card falls back to the old string parse, so SEQ-18 is unclosed on a real host.

HARNESS CORRECTION the charter's item 4 wording depends on: `tree` can NEVER print [DISABLED] for a Flutter button -- it prints the flag only when a node is interactive and carries neither `enabled` nor `sensitive`, and a disabled Flutter button publishes ['sensitive','showing','visible']. I therefore probed AT-SPI directly and, crucially, probed the ACTION list, which is what the F-fix changed. Disabled pre-flight Start: states=['sensitive','showing','visible'], actions=[], name='Start Sequence -- unavailable: fix the 1 pre-flight error above first'. Disabled Pause under the built-in guider: same signature, name carries the PHD2-only reason. Control experiments in the same dialogs: Re-check and (warnings-only) Start Anyway both give ['enabled','focusable','sensitive','showing','visible'] + actions=['Tap','Focus'], and the same Start button round-trips between the two signatures. Reusable probe left at /tmp/ns-audit/probe_actions.py (name substring + optional pid).

D-2 settled by counting rather than by looking: `tree --all | grep -c 'Projection: Stereographic'` = 1 never-hovered, 1 during a 3 s hover, 1 with the pointer parked away for 8 s. The single occurrence is the BUTTON's accessible name (the fix put the name on the Icon and emptied the Material tooltip message, so no tooltip node is ever created) -- Wave F's 0-then-1-forever signature is gone in both directions.

WF-SCI-N2 was settled against the database, not the screen: Refresh on session 1 wrote a NEW night_reports row (id 2, +47 s) where Wave F's decisive negative was that the table stayed at one row; and session 2 (6 subs) reads 70/100 'Rough night: every sub was graded poor.' while session 1 still reads 'Not graded -- only 3 light frames...'. Disclosed as NOT exercised: the 'stored report predates a sub it claims to judge' arm, because adding subs to an already-reported session is not reachable from the GUI (a re-run opens a new session).

SAME-CLASS FINDING, different surface, not double-filed: Analytics -> History -> session card -- the icon-row tooltips 'Review & Integrate' and 'Session Report' stay in the a11y tree after the pointer leaves and accumulate as the pointer sweeps the row. That is D-2's shape on a surface D-2's fix did not touch.

Two more notes for whoever drives next: (1) wait 5 s before judging a toast stack (see WD-EQ-3); (2) 'the dashboard scrolled to the bottom' is ambiguous -- standby has two content branches (briefing with the Moon card when nothing is connected, connected-idle with Mount/Safety/Recent events otherwise) and a finding has to name which.
